# Conformance skill

payloadFields.reason: The domain selector. It is a constant chosen from the registry BEFORE any other payload field is read, so it can never disagree with the assessment.
A constant of the attestation format, decided before any other field is read; it says nothing about the assessment.
The signer namespace claim. It scopes key-set lookup and retained sequence state; it is not a property of the assessment.
A constant naming the canonicalization the digest used; there is exactly one admitted value, so nothing can differ.
Context only: the workspace the signing service acted for. Not derivable from the assessment, and never a verification restriction.
Bound to the embedded public key by the keyId derivation check, and to the key set by lookup; it is not derivable from the assessment.
The signer's claimed time. It is not trusted time and is compared to nothing but a verifier-supplied policy clock.

cases.name: bundle-version.unsupported."1.1.0"
cases.description: bundleVersion "1.1.0" is UNSUPPORTED_BUNDLE_VERSION. It is unsigned, so this is NOT INVALID_SIGNATURE: changing it can only make a verifier refuse.

cases.name: bundle-version.decided-first
cases.description: A future bundleVersion with unknown fields, a missing assessment and a broken attestation is still UNSUPPORTED_BUNDLE_VERSION: the version is decided before anything else is read.

cases.name: bundle-version.independent-of-attestation-version
cases.description: Nothing links the two versions: bundleVersion 1.0.0 with an attestationVersion this verifier does not support is UNSUPPORTED_VERSION (see strict.version-1.1.0), and an unsupported bundleVersion with a supported attestation is UNSUPPORTED_BUNDLE_VERSION.

cases.name: tamper.payload.keyId

cases.description: issuedAt changed by one second after signing

cases.name: tamper.payload.workspace.added
cases.description: a workspaceId added to a bundle that was signed without one

cases.name: tamper.payload.workspace.removed
cases.description: the workspaceId removed from a bundle that was signed with one

cases.name: tamper.payload.workspace.changed
cases.description: the workspaceId changed on a bundle that was signed with another

cases.name: tamper.signature.bit-flipped
cases.description: one bit of the signature flipped (the result is either still low-S and fails verification, or fails the form check; see signature.* for the form rules)

cases.name: tamper.signature.from-another-bundle
cases.description: the signature of a different bundle (B2) on this payload

cases.name: tamper.publicKey.swapped-keyId-unchanged
cases.description: the embedded key replaced by an attacker key while keyId still names the original: keyId no longer matches the embedded key

cases.name: tamper.publicKey.and-keyId-swapped
cases.description: the embedded key AND the payload keyId both replaced by the attacker key: consistent, but the signature was made by another key

cases.name: cross-type.untagged-signature
cases.description: A signature over the untagged JCS bytes does not verify against the tagged signing input, even with the right key.

cases.name: signature.high-s-twin
cases.description: The valid signature (r, s) turned into its twin (r, n - s). It is a mathematically valid signature; the profile type refuses it. Legacy verification is unchanged and accepts both forms (see the legacy vectors).

cases.name: signature.high-s-boundary-plus-one
cases.description: s = floor(n/2) + 1, the smallest rejected value. Rejected on FORM, before any cryptography.

cases.name: signature.low-s-boundary-inclusive
cases.description: s = floor(n/2), the largest admitted value: admitted on form, and then (not being a real signature) INVALID_SIGNATURE. Pins that the boundary is inclusive.

cases.name: signature.s-one
cases.description: s = 1, the smallest admitted value: admitted on form, INVALID_SIGNATURE.

cases.name: signature.s-zero
cases.description: s = 0 is out of range.

cases.name: signature.r-zero
cases.description: r = 0 is out of range.

cases.name: signature.r-equals-n
cases.description: r = n is out of range.

cases.name: signature.s-equals-n
cases.description: s = n is out of range (range is checked before low-S, so this is not reported as high-S).

cases.name: signature.r-max
cases.description: r = 2^256 - 1 is out of range.

cases.name: signature.s-max
cases.description: s = 2^256 - 1 is out of range.

cases.name: signature.r-just-below-n
cases.description: r = n - 1 is in range (and, not being a real signature, INVALID_SIGNATURE).

cases.name: signature.high-s-twin.workspace-bundle
cases.description: The same rule on the workspace bundle.

cases.name: signature.form-checked-before-key-id
cases.description: The signature form is checked before the key id: a high-S signature on a bundle whose keyId is also wrong is reported as high-S.

cases.description: issuedAt without milliseconds is rejected: one canonical spelling per instant.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-offset
cases.description: issuedAt with a numeric offset is rejected.

cases.name: strict.canonicalization-name
cases.description: assessment.canonicalization other than RFC8785 is rejected.

cases.name: strict.profile-id-format
cases.description: A profile id that is not lowercase words joined by hyphens is rejected.

cases.name: strict.type-null
cases.description: attestationType: null is malformed, not legacy.

cases.name: strict.type-unknown
cases.description: An unknown attestationType is UNSUPPORTED_TYPE, with no partial verification.

cases.name: strict.version-1.1.0
cases.description: attestationVersion 1.1.0 is UNSUPPORTED_VERSION, checked before any other payload field.

cases.name: strict.version-2.0.0
cases.description: attestationVersion 2.0.0 is UNSUPPORTED_VERSION.

cases.name: strict.version-and-unknown-field
cases.description: A future version that also carries unknown fields is still UNSUPPORTED_VERSION: the version is decided first.

cases.name: interpretation.future-schema
cases.description: Integrity is still VALID (the digest is over opaque JSON), but interpretation is UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA: show raw JSON only, never a rendered status.

cases.name: interpretation.schema-decided-before-profile
cases.description: An unsupported schema is reported as UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA, not UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE: the schema is decided first.

cases.name: interpretation.unknown-profile
cases.description: INTEGRITY is VALID (never INVALID_SIGNATURE); INTERPRETATION is UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE. Nothing may be rendered or concluded from it.

cases.name: interpretation.unknown-profile-version
cases.description: Known profile, unknown profile version: INTEGRITY VALID, INTERPRETATION UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE_VERSION.

cases.name: interpretation.framework-not-pinned
cases.description: CHANGED FROM v2 (was UNSUPPORTED_PROFILE): the profile id and version are known but the framework differs from the pinned definition: PROFILE_DEFINITION_MISMATCH, reason profile.framework.

cases.name: interpretation.registry-is-closed
cases.description: profile "constructor" is unknown, not inherited from Object.prototype.

cases.name: interpretation.unsupported-never-invalid-signature
cases.description: An unsupported interpretation is never turned into INVALID_SIGNATURE: the same signature verifies whether or not this verifier can read the assessment.

cases.name: malformed.payload-field-missing
cases.description: issuedAt removed

cases.name: malformed.version-missing
cases.description: attestationVersion removed

cases.name: malformed.type-missing
cases.description: attestationType removed from a payload INSIDE a bundle: a bundle never carries a legacy attestation, so this is malformed rather than routed

cases.name: malformed.fileCount-string
cases.description: package.fileCount as a string

cases.name: malformed.fileCount-negative
cases.description: package.fileCount negative

cases.name: malformed.implementedControls-string
cases.description: implementedControls as a string

cases.name: malformed.implementedControls-duplicate
cases.description: implementedControls containing a duplicate

cases.name: malformed.package-digest-prefix
cases.description: package digest with the OWASP-style sha256: prefix instead of avpkg-sha256:

cases.name: malformed.assessment-digest-uppercase
cases.description: assessment digest in uppercase hex

cases.name: malformed.commit-short
cases.description: OWASP commit shorter than 40 hex characters

cases.name: malformed.profileVersion-not-semver
cases.description: profileVersion not a semantic version

cases.name: malformed.keyId-shape
cases.description: keyId not 43 base64url characters

cases.name: malformed.attestation-unknown-field
cases.description: an unknown field on the attestation object

cases.name: malformed.bundle-unknown-field
cases.description: an unknown field on the bundle

cases.name: malformed.bundle-assessment-missing
cases.description: the assessment removed from the bundle

cases.name: malformed.assessment-not-object
cases.description: the assessment replaced by an array

cases.name: malformed.algorithm-missing
cases.description: the algorithm removed

cases.name: malformed.signature-empty
cases.description: an empty signature

cases.name: malformed.signature-not-base64
cases.description: a signature that is not base64

cases.name: malformed.signature-truncated
cases.description: a truncated signature

cases.name: malformed.signature-unpadded
cases.description: a signature without its base64 padding (one canonical encoding only)

cases.name: malformed.signature-with-whitespace
cases.description: a signature with a newline inside it

cases.name: malformed.signature-wrong-length
cases.description: a 32-byte value that is valid base64

cases.name: malformed.publicKey-private-material
cases.description: an embedded key carrying private material (d)

cases.name: malformed.publicKey-extra-member
cases.description: an embedded key with WebCrypto-style extra members (ext, key_ops): the new type is stricter than the legacy one

cases.name: malformed.publicKey-coordinate-length
cases.description: an embedded key with a short x coordinate

cases.name: malformed.publicKey-coordinate-padded
cases.description: an embedded key whose x is padded with "=" (44 characters)

cases.name: malformed.publicKey-x-noncanonical
cases.description: an embedded key whose x is a NON-CANONICAL spelling of the same 32 bytes: the same key would otherwise get a second keyId

cases.name: malformed.publicKey-y-noncanonical
cases.description: the same for y

cases.name: malformed.publicKey-not-object
cases.description: an embedded key that is a string

cases.name: unsupported.algorithm-name
cases.description: algorithm ES256 (a real JOSE name, but not this verifier's)

cases.name: unsupported.curve
cases.description: an embedded P-384 key

cases.name: malformed.publicKey-not-on-curve
cases.description: a well-shaped, canonical key that is not a point on P-256 (payload keyId set to its thumbprint so the check is reached)

cases.description: a duplicate key in the payload

cases.name: unicode.nfc-and-nfd-are-distinct
cases.description: NFC and NFD spellings are different keys and different strings: both are kept, neither is normalized, and the bundle verifies.

cases.name: unicode.normalizing-a-value-changes-the-digest
cases.description: Replacing a path with its canonically equivalent NFD spelling is a DIFFERENT assessment: the digest no longer matches. (A verifier that normalized would have accepted it.)

cases.name: unicode.swapping-the-two-spellings-changes-the-digest
cases.description: Exchanging the two spellings inside the string array is a different assessment.

cases.name: key-state.no-key-set
cases.description: With no key set the result is explicitly NOT_EVALUATED: internal consistency only. There is no "trusted" state anywhere.

cases.name: key-state.active
cases.description: Listed as an active key for the profile purpose in the supplied key set. This records what the key set says; it is not a trust decision.

cases.name: key-state.retired.issuedAt-after-retiredAt
cases.description: The key set records the key as retired on 2026-01-10; the payload CLAIMS issuedAt 2026-01-15. The state is KEY_RETIRED. No anomaly is flagged and nothing is concluded about when the signature was really made.

cases.name: key-state.retired.issuedAt-before-retiredAt
cases.description: The key set records the key as retired on 2026-02-01; the payload claims issuedAt 2026-01-15. Also KEY_RETIRED: identical to the other order, so no time inference is made either way. issuedAt is a signer claim, not trusted time.

cases.name: key-state.rotated-in-active
cases.description: The same content signed by the rotated-in key, which is active.

cases.name: key-state.revoked.revokedAt-after-issuedAt
cases.description: Revoked on 2026-01-20; claimed issuedAt is earlier. KEY_REVOKED regardless: after a compromise every signature under the key is suspect, whatever it says about time.

cases.name: key-state.revoked.revokedAt-before-issuedAt
cases.description: Revoked on 2026-01-01; claimed issuedAt is later. KEY_REVOKED, identically.

cases.name: key-state.purpose-mismatch
cases.description: The key is in the key set but declared for another purpose: KEY_PURPOSE_MISMATCH, distinct from a bad signature and from an unknown key. Integrity is unaffected.

cases.name: key-state.purpose-checked-before-revocation
cases.description: A revoked key with the wrong purpose reports KEY_PURPOSE_MISMATCH: the purpose is checked first. (Both are refused by every policy.)

cases.name: key-state.purpose-checked-before-retirement
cases.description: A retired key with the wrong purpose reports KEY_PURPOSE_MISMATCH, not KEY_RETIRED.

cases.name: key-state.unknown-key
cases.description: keyId absent from the key set.

cases.name: key-state.self-signed-attacker
cases.description: An internally consistent bundle signed by a key nobody published.

cases.name: key-state.issuer-mismatch
cases.description: Payload issuer is not the key set's issuer namespace.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.missing-purpose
cases.description: A key set entry with no purpose is not a usable key set: purpose must be explicit.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.keyId-mismatch
cases.description: A key set entry whose keyId is not the thumbprint of its own key.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.duplicate
cases.description: Two key set entries with the same keyId.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.private-material
cases.description: A key set entry carrying private key material.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.bad-status
cases.description: A key set entry with an unknown status.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.retired-without-date
cases.description: A retired entry without retiredAt.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.unknown-field
cases.description: A key set entry with an unknown field.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.non-canonical-coordinate
cases.description: A key set entry whose x is a non-canonical spelling: one key, one accepted spelling, one keyId.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.unknown-version
cases.description: An unknown keySetVersion fails closed.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.missing-sequence
cases.description: A key set without a sequence.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.sequence-zero
cases.description: sequence must be a positive integer.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.sequence-string
cases.description: sequence must be an integer, not a string.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.bad-generatedAt
cases.description: generatedAt must be a canonical timestamp (it is informational, but its form is strict).

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.unknown-top-level-field
cases.description: An unknown field on the key set itself.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.entry-purpose-empty
cases.description: A key set entry whose purpose is present but EMPTY: purpose must be explicit and non-empty.

cases.name: key-state.key-set-invalid.entry-notBefore-not-canonical
cases.description: A key set entry whose notBefore is not a canonical timestamp (2026-01-01 instead of 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z).

cases.name: key-state.rollback.stale-key-set-for-the-correct-issuer
cases.description: The verifier retained sequence 5 FOR THIS ISSUER (agentverify-conformance, the issuer named in the bundle's own payload) and is offered a key set with sequence 3: KEY_SET_ROLLBACK_DETECTED. This is rollback DETECTION, and it works only because the verifier retained prior state for this issuer.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.sequence-equal-to-retained
cases.description: The same sequence as retained (7) is not behind it. The check says NOT_BEHIND_RETAINED: "not older than something already seen", which is not freshness.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.sequence-above-retained
cases.description: A higher sequence than retained is not behind it.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.no-retained-state
cases.description: No retained state at all: the result says NO_RETAINED_STATE. The sequence could not be checked, and that is NOT the same as "sequence confirmed": a verifier with no state learns nothing from the number.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.empty-retained-state
cases.description: An empty retained-state object is the same as none.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.low-sequence-with-no-state-is-accepted
cases.description: The same low-sequence (3) key set with no retained state is simply used, and reported as NO_RETAINED_STATE. The numbers alone protect nothing.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.other-issuers-state-is-ignored
cases.description: Retained state exists, but only for ANOTHER issuer (agentverify-other, sequence 99). It cannot affect this bundle: NO_RETAINED_STATE, and the low-sequence key set is not flagged.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.only-the-payload-issuer-counts
cases.description: Retained state for two issuers: the unrelated one (99) is ignored and the payload issuer's own (2) is used: not behind.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.issuer-a-state-cannot-affect-issuer-b
cases.description: A bundle issued under agentverify-other, with its own key set (sequence 2). Issuer A's retained sequence (99) cannot affect it.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.issuer-b-own-state-applies
cases.description: The same issuer-B bundle, with retained state for issuer B (5): now the stale key set is detected.

cases.name: key-state.rollback.key-set-for-another-issuer-consults-no-state
cases.description: A key set whose issuer is not the payload's issuer is not this issuer's key set: KEY_UNKNOWN, and NO retained state is consulted (no sequence check is reported).

cases.name: key-state.rollback.issuer-named-like-a-prototype-member
cases.description: An issuer literally named "constructor": retained state is read by OWN key only, so an empty state object has nothing for it (an inherited lookup would return a function).

cases.name: key-state.rollback.prototype-named-issuer-with-real-state
cases.description: The same issuer with real retained state (9): it is used, and the key set (sequence 4) is behind it.

cases.name: key-state.not-evaluated-when-integrity-fails
cases.description: Key state is never evaluated for a bundle whose integrity failed, even with a matching key set.

cases.name: policy.satisfied
cases.description: A policy that the bundle satisfies (default: only KEY_ACTIVE is accepted).

cases.name: policy.wrong-profile
cases.description: A different profile was required.

cases.name: policy.commit-not-allowed
cases.description: The OWASP commit is not in the verifier's allowed list.

cases.name: policy.downgrade
cases.description: DOWNGRADE DEFENCE (two independent gates): an attestation that implements only AST03 fails the pinned profile definition (interpretation) AND the verifier required controls.

cases.name: policy.package-digest-mismatch
cases.description: The package on disk is not the one assessed.

cases.name: policy.fresh-enough
cases.description: Within the maximum age (verifier-supplied clock).

cases.name: policy.too-old
cases.description: Older than the maximum age.

cases.name: policy.retired-refused-by-default
cases.description: The reference default accepts KEY_ACTIVE only: a retired key is refused unless the policy opts in.

cases.name: policy.retired-opt-in.issuedAt-after-retiredAt
cases.description: Historical or offline verification explicitly opts into KEY_RETIRED. This is a policy choice, and says nothing about when the signature was made.

cases.name: policy.retired-opt-in.issuedAt-before-retiredAt
cases.description: The same opt-in with the dates the other way round: the same result.

cases.name: policy.revoked-never-accepted
cases.description: KEY_REVOKED is never accepted, even with valid signature mathematics and a policy that accepts everything acceptable.

cases.name: policy.invalid-lists-revoked
cases.description: A policy that LISTS KEY_REVOKED as acceptable is invalid, and fails closed.

cases.name: policy.invalid-empty
cases.description: An empty acceptedKeyStates is invalid.

cases.name: policy.invalid-unknown-state
cases.description: A state that is not an acceptable key state (there is no TRUSTED state) is invalid.

cases.name: policy.invalid-lists-unknown-key
cases.description: KEY_UNKNOWN cannot be listed as acceptable either.

cases.name: policy.no-key-set-fails-default
cases.description: Without a key set the key state is NOT_EVALUATED, which no policy accepts.

cases.name: policy.purpose-mismatch-refused
cases.description: KEY_PURPOSE_MISMATCH is refused by every policy.

cases.name: policy.rollback-detected-refused
cases.description: KEY_SET_ROLLBACK_DETECTED is refused by every policy.

cases.name: policy.unsupported-profile-cannot-satisfy
cases.description: Unknown profile fails closed for any security conclusion: integrity is VALID and the key is active, but the policy is NOT satisfied.

cases.name: policy.unsupported-profile-version-cannot-satisfy
cases.description: Unknown profile version fails closed for any security conclusion.

cases.name: policy.unsupported-schema-cannot-satisfy
cases.description: Unknown assessment schema fails closed for any security conclusion.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-feb-30
cases.description: issuedAt "2026-02-30T00:00:00.000Z": February 30 does not exist (Date.parse-style parsers roll it into March). Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-apr-31
cases.description: issuedAt "2026-04-31T00:00:00.000Z": April has 30 days. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-jun-31
cases.description: issuedAt "2026-06-31T00:00:00.000Z": June has 30 days. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-feb-29-non-leap
cases.description: issuedAt "2025-02-29T00:00:00.000Z": February 29 in a common year. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-feb-29-century-non-leap
cases.description: issuedAt "2100-02-29T00:00:00.000Z": 2100 is divisible by 100 but not 400, so it is not a leap year. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-hour-24
cases.description: issuedAt "2026-01-15T24:00:00.000Z": 24:00 is not admitted (some parsers roll it to the next day). Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-leap-second
cases.description: issuedAt "2026-06-30T23:59:60.000Z": a leap second (:60) is not admitted. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-minute-60
cases.description: issuedAt "2026-01-15T12:60:00.000Z": minute 60. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-month-13
cases.description: issuedAt "2026-13-01T00:00:00.000Z": month 13. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-month-00
cases.description: issuedAt "2026-00-10T00:00:00.000Z": month 00. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-day-00
cases.description: issuedAt "2026-01-00T00:00:00.000Z": day 00. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-year-0000
cases.description: issuedAt "0000-01-01T00:00:00.000Z": year 0000 is outside the admitted 0001-9999 range. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-lowercase-t-z
cases.description: issuedAt "2026-01-15t12:00:00.000z": lowercase T and Z. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-space-separator
cases.description: issuedAt "2026-01-15 12:00:00.000Z": a space instead of T. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-four-fraction-digits
cases.description: issuedAt "2026-01-15T12:00:00.0000Z": four fractional digits. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-expanded-year
cases.description: issuedAt "+002026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z": an expanded year with a sign. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-trailing-space
cases.description: issuedAt "2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z ": trailing whitespace. Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: strict.issuedAt-fullwidth-digits
cases.description: issuedAt "２０２６-01-15T12:00:00.000Z": fullwidth digits (Date and regex \d may disagree about these). Rejected by the one strict timestamp parser, not by Date.parse.

cases.name: timestamp.valid.leap-day
cases.description: issuedAt 2024-02-29T12:00:00.000Z (February 29 in a leap year) is admitted.

cases.name: timestamp.valid.century-leap-day
cases.description: issuedAt 2000-02-29T12:00:00.000Z (2000 is divisible by 400, so it is a leap year) is admitted.

cases.name: timestamp.valid.last-instant
cases.description: issuedAt 9999-12-31T23:59:59.999Z (the largest admitted instant) is admitted.

cases.name: timestamp.valid.first-instant
cases.description: issuedAt 0001-01-01T00:00:00.000Z (the smallest admitted instant) is admitted.

cases.name: binding.signer-lied.package.fileCount.assessment-has-a-string
cases.description: A number in the payload and the same digits as a STRING in the assessment are not the same value: BINDING_MISMATCH on package.fileCount (no loose equality).

cases.name: binding.signer-lied.implementedControls.assessment-has-a-string
cases.description: An array and its comma-joined string are not the same value: BINDING_MISMATCH on implementedControls.

cases.name: malformed.signature-trailing-bits-alias
cases.description: One unused trailing bit set in the last base64 character: a lenient decoder reads exactly the same 64 bytes (so the same valid signature), but the spelling is not canonical: refused.

cases.name: malformed.signature-trailing-bits-alias-all-set
cases.description: All four unused trailing bits set: the same 64 bytes, a different spelling, refused.

cases.name: malformed.signature-extra-padding
cases.description: The canonical text plus one more "=".

cases.name: malformed.signature-single-padding
cases.description: Only one "=" of padding where two are required.

cases.name: malformed.signature-url-safe-alphabet-character
cases.description: A character from the URL-safe alphabet ("-") where the standard alphabet is required.

cases.name: malformed.signature-url-safe-underscore
cases.description: The other URL-safe character ("_").

cases.name: malformed.signature-leading-space
cases.description: A leading space.

cases.name: malformed.signature-not-a-string
cases.description: A number where the signature string belongs.

cases.name: malformed.signature-null
cases.description: null where the signature belongs.

cases.name: unsupported-schema.payload-disagrees
cases.description: An unsupported schema that also disagrees with the payload: the schemaVersion cross-check runs for EVERY schema, so this is BINDING_MISMATCH (not UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA): the signer contradicted itself.

cases.name: unsupported-schema.payload-claims-future-assessment-supported
cases.description: The mirror image: BINDING_MISMATCH on assessmentSchemaVersion.

cases.name: unsupported-schema.structure-check-skipped.profile
cases.description: Under an unsupported schema the structure-dependent cross-check for the payload profile id is SKIPPED (the structure cannot be read), so integrity is VALID and the interpretation is UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA. The same lie under a SUPPORTED schema is BINDING_MISMATCH (see binding.signer-lied.*).

cases.name: unsupported-schema.structure-check-skipped.upstream-commit
cases.description: Under an unsupported schema the structure-dependent cross-check for the payload upstream commit is SKIPPED (the structure cannot be read), so integrity is VALID and the interpretation is UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA. The same lie under a SUPPORTED schema is BINDING_MISMATCH (see binding.signer-lied.*).

cases.name: unsupported-schema.structure-check-skipped.implemented-controls

The same lie under a SUPPORTED schema is BINDING_MISMATCH (see binding.signer-lied.*).

cases.name: unsupported-schema.structure-check-skipped.package-digest

The same lie under a SUPPORTED schema is BINDING_MISMATCH (see binding.signer-lied.*).

cases.name: unsupported-schema.structure-check-skipped.interpretation-version

The same lie under a SUPPORTED schema is BINDING_MISMATCH (see binding.signer-lied.*).

cases.name: unsupported-schema.digest-still-checked
cases.description: The digest binding is never skipped: changing an unsupported-schema assessment after signing is BINDING_MISMATCH on the digest.

cases.name: depth.bundle-root-counts
cases.description: Depth is measured from the bundle root, not from the assessment: an object nested 63 levels under the bundle ROOT itself is depth 64 and parses (unknown top-level field => MALFORMED bundle.shape); 64 levels is depth 65 and does not parse.

cases.name: depth.bundle-root-over
cases.description: One level deeper than the previous vector.

cases.name: bytes.valid-multibyte-equals-text
cases.description: The base bundle as raw UTF-8 bytes (it contains 2-byte, 3-byte and 4-byte sequences: é, ～ and 🙂). Same result as the text and object forms.

cases.name: bytes.invalid-utf8.stray-continuation
cases.description: A lone continuation byte (0x80) inside a string. A lenient decoder substitutes U+FFFD and continues; the verifier refuses the bytes.

cases.name: bytes.invalid-utf8.invalid-second-byte
cases.description: 0xC3 followed by an ASCII byte (a truncated 2-byte sequence).

cases.name: bytes.invalid-utf8.overlong
cases.description: The overlong encoding C0 AF of "/".

cases.name: bytes.invalid-utf8.encoded-surrogate
cases.description: ED A0 80: a UTF-8 encoding of the lone surrogate U+D800 (WTF-8 / CESU-style). Not well-formed UTF-8.

cases.name: bytes.invalid-utf8.truncated-four-byte
cases.description: F0 9F 98 followed by the closing quote: a 4-byte sequence cut short.

cases.name: bytes.invalid-utf8.above-max-code-point
cases.description: F4 90 80 80 is U+110000, above the Unicode maximum.

cases.name: bytes.invalid-utf8.byte-ff
cases.description: The byte 0xFF, which never occurs in UTF-8.

cases.name: bytes.invalid-utf8.in-a-key
cases.description: Invalid UTF-8 inside an object key rather than a value.

cases.name: bytes.bom
cases.description: A UTF-8 byte order mark (EF BB BF) before the JSON. One accepted transport encoding: no BOM.

cases.name: bytes.bom-only
cases.description: A byte order mark and nothing else.

cases.name: bytes.feff-inside-a-string-is-a-character
cases.description: U+FEFF INSIDE a string is an ordinary character and is not stripped: the assessment text changed, so the digest no longer matches. (A decoder that stripped every U+FEFF would report VALID.)

cases.name: bytes.utf16-le-ascii-is-not-json
cases.description: ASCII JSON encoded as UTF-16LE (no BOM): the interleaved NUL bytes are valid UTF-8 but are not JSON.

cases.name: bytes.utf16-le-with-bom
cases.description: UTF-16LE with its byte order mark FF FE: 0xFF never occurs in UTF-8.

cases.name: bytes.empty
cases.description: Zero bytes.

cases.name: bytes.nul-byte-in-string
cases.description: A raw NUL byte inside a string is an unescaped control character.

cases.name: bytes.valid-utf8-lone-surrogate-escape
cases.description: Well-formed UTF-8 bytes containing the ESCAPE \ud800: the bytes are valid, the JSON string is ill-formed.

cases.description: age == maxAgeSeconds satisfies the bound (the boundary is INCLUSIVE): issuedAt 12:00:00.000, now 13:00:00.000, max 3600.

cases.name: policy.age.one-millisecond-over-fails
cases.description: age one millisecond over the maximum fails: the comparison is on exact milliseconds.

cases.name: policy.age.one-second-over-fails
cases.description: age one SECOND over the maximum fails.

cases.name: policy.age.zero-max-age-same-instant
cases.description: maxAgeSeconds 0 with now == issuedAt: age 0 <= 0, satisfied.

cases.name: policy.age.zero-max-age-one-millisecond

cases.name: policy.age.future-issuedAt-fails

cases.name: policy.age.future-issuedAt-huge-window-still-fails
cases.description: A huge (but valid) maxAgeSeconds does not rescue a future issuedAt.

cases.name: policy.age.huge-window-old-bundle-satisfied
cases.description: The largest safe integer as the window: any real age satisfies it (and nothing overflows).

cases.name: policy.age.missing-now
